questions.text: Which term refers to the high-level structure of a system, including how it is broken into components and how those components communicate with each other?
questions.hint: This is the 'blueprint' of a program, made before heavy coding begins.

questions.text: What is the primary difference between Program Architecture and Project/System Architecture?
options: Program architecture is about hardware; project architecture is about software
Program architecture focuses on internal code organization; project architecture focuses on how multiple systems interact
Program architecture is only for monoliths; project architecture is only for microservices
There is no difference; they are interchangeable terms
questions.hint: Consider the scope: one is inside a single application, the other is the bigger picture.

questions.text: Which design principle states that each part of a system should handle one specific responsibility and not mix unrelated concerns?
questions.hint: This principle prevents mixing database code with UI code.

questions.text: The SOLID principles are primarily associated with which programming paradigm?
questions.hint: These are common in OOP-based backend design like Java or C#.

questions.text: In the Client-Server model, what is the role of the client?
options: To store and manage persistent data
To process business logic and validate requests
To request and display data to the user
questions.hint: The client is typically a browser, mobile app, or desktop application.

questions.text: Which tier in a Three-Tier Architecture is responsible for business rules, processing, and validation?
questions.hint: This tier is where Node.js/Express, Django, or Laravel would run.

questions.text: What is the primary advantage of using a 3-Tier or N-Tier architecture over a 2-tier architecture?
options: It provides better separation of concerns and independent scalability
It eliminates the need for a database
questions.hint: Think about the benefits of separating UI, logic, and data layers.

questions.text: In the MVC (Model-View-Controller) pattern, which component is responsible for handling user input and coordinating the Model and View?
questions.hint: This component acts as the intermediary between the user interface and the data.

questions.text: Which popular web frameworks use the MVC pattern? (Select the best answer)
questions.hint: Think about frameworks that follow a server-side Model-View-Controller pattern.

questions.text: Which architectural pattern is commonly used in modern frontend frameworks like Vue and Angular, and features two-way data binding?
questions.hint: This pattern has a ViewModel that binds the Model to the View automatically.

questions.text: What is a key characteristic of a Monolithic Architecture?
options: The application is split into small, independent services
The entire application is built and deployed as one single unit
It uses an Enterprise Service Bus for communication
questions.hint: This is the traditional approach where UI, business logic, and data access are all in one codebase.

questions.text: Which architecture splits an application into small, independent services that communicate via APIs and can be deployed separately?
questions.hint: Each service in this architecture is responsible for one business capability.

questions.text: How do Microservices typically differ from Service-Oriented Architecture (SOA)?
options: Microservices are larger and more coarse-grained
Microservices are smaller, more independent, and each usually owns its own database
questions.hint: Consider the size and independence of the services in each approach.

questions.text: Which architecture uses cloud provider-managed functions that automatically scale and do not require server management?
questions.hint: AWS Lambda and Azure Functions are examples of this architecture.

questions.text: In a RESTful API, which HTTP method is used to create a new resource?
questions.hint: This method is typically used when submitting a form to add new data.

questions.text: Which integration style uses XML and is more common in older enterprise banking systems?
questions.hint: This protocol is stricter than REST and often uses XML envelopes.

questions.text: What is the primary advantage of GraphQL compared to REST?
options: It is faster than REST for all operations
It allows clients to specify exactly what data they need in a single query
It uses XML instead of JSON
questions.hint: This allows the client to request only the data they need, reducing over-fetching.

questions.text: In Event-Driven Architecture, what is the role of a Message Broker?
options: To route events from producers to consumers
questions.hint: Kafka and RabbitMQ are examples of this component.

questions.text: Which architecture is best suited for small applications, MVPs, and small teams due to its simplicity?
questions.hint: This is the simplest and most straightforward architecture to start with.

questions.text: Which architecture offers excellent scalability and allows different parts of the system to use different tech stacks?
questions.hint: This architecture is designed for large, complex, evolving systems.

questions.text: The DRY principle stands for 'Don't Repeat Yourself' and encourages centralizing logic to avoid duplication.
questions.hint: This principle helps reduce redundancy and improve maintainability.

questions.text: In a Microservices Architecture, all services typically share a single centralized database.
questions.hint: Each service usually owns its own database for independence.

questions.text: The layer in a Three-Tier Architecture that handles storage and retrieval of data is called the _______ tier.
questions.hint: This tier typically uses databases like MySQL, PostgreSQL, or MongoDB.

questions.text: In the MVC pattern, the component that represents the user interface and displays data is the _______.
questions.hint: This is what the user sees and interacts with.

questions.text: A persistent two-way connection for real-time communication (e.g., chat or live dashboards) uses the _______ protocol.
questions.hint: This protocol enables full-duplex communication between client and server.

questions.text: The design principle that states components should depend on each other as little as possible is called _______.
questions.hint: This ensures changing one component doesn't break another.

questions.text: The architectural style where code runs in stateless functions managed by a cloud provider without server management is called _______.
questions.hint: AWS Lambda and Azure Functions are examples of this approach.

questions.text: In RESTful APIs, the address used to uniquely identify a resource (e.g., /api/users/123) is called a _______.
questions.hint: This is a Uniform Resource Identifier that points to a specific resource.

questions.text: The integration pattern where components communicate by producing and reacting to events through a message broker is called _______.
questions.hint: This is often used for real-time, decoupled systems.

questions.text: The architectural principle that code should be grouped logically with related code is called _______.
questions.hint: This keeps related logic together and improves maintainability.
